invariants: Off-screen draw suppression must survive. Today the shell stamps data-onscreen on each iframe's <html> and dispatches 'midi-studio:onscreen'; an iframe cannot detect occlusion itself (document.hidden tracks only the window) and backgroundThrottling:false + disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows + disable-renderer-backgrounding mean the platform never throttles a hidden panel. If iframes become in-document panels, replace it with one visibility scheduler every canvas loop subscribes to. Drop it and every hidden tab burns GPU forever.

The draw budget (data-drawms), the 'game is running' multiplier and the 'window unfocused' penalty must stay three separate inputs. A past bug folded user preference and gameActive into one flag and latched the limit on permanently the first time Roblox was seen. A game may RAISE the budget (x3), never lower or overwrite the user's percent. The three must never compound (that landed at 5fps and made the roll teleport).

While playback is live the Player's budget is floored at >=30fps (min(base,33)). Playing into a game means this window is normally NOT focused, so unfocused is the usual case and never a reason to go choppy.

Ctrl+1..N tab switching must be caught in the MAIN process via before-input-event as well as in the shell. The stage covers almost the whole window and swallows keydowns once focus is inside a tab. Extend both maps to 5 tabs together or they disagree.

webContents.send reaches only the main frame. engine-event/engine-error/forge:status/library-changed/game-active/overlay-state/overlay-wants-state must go through broadcast() (walk mainFrame.framesInSubtree, then send separately to the Perch window, which the frame walk cannot reach). update-status/shell-shortcut/open-midi must stay main-frame-only so exactly one update banner exists.

Playback ALWAYS backgrounds Forge (a late keypress is audibly wrong and cannot be caught up); a detected game only backgrounds Forge when whenGaming!=='nothing'. playbackActive and gameUp stay separate flags so one ending does not cancel the other. OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE + KMP_BLOCKTIME=0 + OMP_NUM_THREADS are what make 'go easy' mean anything, because Torch's OpenMP pool spin-waits and never yields.

The Forge pipeline output pump must split on \r as well as \n. MSST tqdm and yt-dlp rewrite one line with \r and never send \n; newline-only splitting showed nothing for the longest part of a run. Progress percent stays monotonic (peak = Math.max) and the keyword fallback must keep skipping lines starting with 'input:' (the 'Input: song.mp3' echo jumped the bar to 90%).

collectAdvanced() must send ALL 23 advanced keys on every write: main deep-merges, so an omitted key keeps its old on-disk value. Empty string means 'engine default'. LEGACY_DEFAULTS (MIN_NOTE_SEC '0.05', MELODY_MIN_NOTE_MS '45') must keep being treated as unset.
selectScript must test pipeline==='fast' BEFORE skipSeparation, or Fast silently routes to Transkun.
forge.run gates on forgeEnvReady (site-packages/torch AND a .ready marker), not merely 'python.exe exists'. A cancelled setup otherwise dies on import.

Orphan-job reaping must stay: a Forge job is a separate python.exe holding the GPU, and a hard kill of the app leaves it transcribing forever. forge-jobs.json also tracks the PLAYER sidecar pid, because a leftover copy inside the install folder makes the next installer refuse to update.

The sidecar must always emit {event:'playback_done',crashed:true} on exit, or Play stays disabled and the queue stays locked until the app restarts. PYTHONPATH=engineDir and MIDI_STUDIO_MAPPINGS_DIR must be set before it spawns.

Empty means UNBOUND for all ten Player hotkeys, including play/pause/stop, so those keys can be freed for the game. Focusing a capture box must suspend global hotkeys or the key being rebound fires its old action.

hand / hand_split / chord_stagger_ms change WHICH notes exist and WHEN they fire, so they must ship with every load_midi, play AND export_sheet or the visualizer, the keys sent and the VP sheet disagree.

A user Stop must always send {cmd:'stop'} even when the UI thinks nothing is playing, so a just-dispatched tempo-restart session dies. userStopped suppresses the queue advance, the sent/dropped summary and the practice loop.

Live tempo change must stop-and-restart at the equivalent musical position (pendingRestartAt = elapsed*prev/next), never just reload the visualizer while the engine keeps the old timeline. When paused it must pre-seek and never auto-resume.

Loading a track is not playing it: starting the engine also focuses the game window, so playback only ever starts on an explicit ask (Play, a row's play button, a hotkey, or the natural end of the previous track).

The visualizer's local extrapolating clock (elapsed = serverSync + wall delta) must stay, or notes teleport between progress packets. Drag-lock must ignore incoming progress packets during a scrub and release only ~250ms after the final seek. A backwards jump >0.2s must reset the cull cursor or notes behind the playhead never reappear.

The editor's roll canvas must stay viewport-sized with a scroll wrapper supplying the extent. A five-minute song at default zoom is ~24,000px, past Chromium's 16,384px limit and 60+MB of pixels, so the tail of a long song simply never drew. Pointer x must be converted back into content space, and the pinned key strip must be drawn last, outside the clip.
The note resize-edge hit zone stays proportional (width>14 && right-x < min(8, width*0.3)). A fixed 8px zone made almost every 1/16 note resize instead of move.
A plain click must never dirty the project or push an undo entry: the checkpoint is deferred to the first >=2px move and confirmed by a real start/end/pitch diff on release.

Undo/redo is keyed by note id (loader 'n1..nN', editor 'add<n>'), never by array index, and note ids must stay stable across clone/restore. The loader's `unterminated:true` flag must round-trip; a fixed-field note constructor silently drops it.

doc.bpm may be an onset-derived guess flagged bpmEstimated, because transcriptions carry no tempo track and mido reports 120 for everything. Quantize snapping to a wrong 120 grid moves every note on a 174 BPM song, so bpm/bpmEstimated must survive save and should now be surfaced with an override.
Opening a plain .mid must leave projectPath empty and must never be saved in place: candidates.clean points at the user's own file. candidateTarget()'s fromProject gate is the protection.
Renaming a project must clear project.candidates so the next save writes new files instead of overwriting the ones the old name pointed at.

Self MIDI playback must stay a lookahead scheduler (notes pinned to the Web Audio clock ~1.5s ahead). A late or throttled wake-up then costs nothing. Never convert it to per-frame note firing. The seamless loop must roll audioStart forward, not call seek().
Canvas backing stores may only be reallocated when the pixel size actually changed; reassigning width/height per frame reallocates and clears the surface and stalls playback.

Split sizes in localStorage 'midi-studio:splits' must be read-merge-written per divider key. Every tab shares one localStorage and a whole-object write erased what the other panes had saved. A divider commit must dispatch a synthetic window 'resize' because several canvases only re-measure on that event.

[hidden]{display:none !important} must stay in the token layer: component display rules (.spane.is-active{display:flex}, .modal-scrim{display:flex}) otherwise beat the hidden attribute and every modal/banner/disclosure breaks at once. button[role=radio|checkbox|switch|tab] must keep appearance:none or Chromium paints a native radio through the label.

Fonts stay bundled woff2 served locally: the page CSP (default-src 'self', script-src 'self') blocks remote anything. No CDN, no inline event handlers. Self MIDI is the one page that deliberately has no strict script-src because soundfont banks are loaded by injecting a <script>.

--text-3 (#868a92) is the AA contrast floor (5.27 on --bg, 4.82 on --surface) and the type scale bottoms out at 12px on purpose; an older 8.5-11.5px band was unreadable at 100% on 1080p. The 9px keyboard label font in the visualizer is the one sanctioned exception.

will-prevent-unload has inverted semantics: preventDefault() means proceed with the close. The Editor's dirty-state beforeunload must keep going through that dialog, or the window silently refuses to close with no escape but Task Manager.

window-all-closed must keep the forced app.exit(0) after 4s, and second-instance must not show a window that has not painted (that white rectangle is what 'it opens white and never loads' was) and must be able to recreate a lost window instead of exiting.

Perch must use setAlwaysOnTop(true,'screen-saver') and showInactive(), never show(): plain alwaysOnTop loses to a borderless-fullscreen game, and taking focus mid-song pauses playback. It must be closed with the main window and in cleanup(), its saved bounds re-validated against the displays that exist now, and overlay-config sent before any queued events.

overlay:replay stays allowlisted to midi_loaded|playback_started|progress, and overlay:command stays allowlisted to the seven transport names, so a compromised frame cannot drive the always-on-top window. Perch owns no playback state: its transport is replayed as a synthetic hotkey so queue/tempo logic lives in exactly one place.

The updater must never pass /S to the NSIS installer (silent mode re-decided the install dir and re-ran the old uninstaller) and on Windows must launch it via Start-Process, never a direct spawn (detached:true does not detach, so the installer taskkilled its own parent tree). Elevate with -Verb RunAs when the install dir is not writable. An absent digest falls back to opening the release page; a digest MISMATCH throws.

adoptInstallerForgePath must never trade a provisioned env for an empty one (the 2.20.0 bug), and recoverForgeEnv must keep repointing at a ready env found elsewhere. cleanReinstall and changeForgeStorage only ever touch our managed env (marker file or default path), never an adopted legacy midi-forge.
Settings deepMerge REPLACES arrays. library.dirs and any new array setting must be written whole.

app:setPerformance must write explicit nulls for advanced.threads/batch when percent is set (deep-merge would keep a hand-set value), and the cleared-override test must check the value, not Number(v), because Number(null)===0 is finite and clearing used to set it to 1.

Fix, do not reproduce: 'HKCU\\Software\\StarsationX\\MIDI Studio' (main.js:522) and 'C:\\Windows' (main.js:500) are written with single backslashes in ordinary string literals, so the escapes collapse and the reg QUERY targets a key that cannot exist while the reg ADD (correctly escaped) writes the real one. Installer-chosen Forge storage is therefore never adopted.

The five-tab nav, the activity strip and the bottom transport are one document's chrome; the bottom transport must have a single explicit owner at a time (Player engine, Self MIDI synth, or Editor preview) with the other two parked, or two clocks and two Space handlers fight.

The postMessage/hand-off router currently does no origin check. All frames are 'self' under the CSP today; if any remote content ever loads, tab switching and file loading become an injection surface.

Needed by forge waveform, editor roll + waveform, player song map + visualizer, self-MIDI roll, library grid sparkline.

top_perf_items.area: Player - full-song overview redraw during playback (renderer/player/app.js:2020, drawRangeOverview)
top_perf_items.issue: Called from the render loop every 80ms while notes are playing and redraws the entire song: up to 6000 fillRect calls plus a getComputedStyle(documentElement) read for --accent per draw. Only the playhead and the range shading actually move.
top_perf_items.fix: Cache the note bars to an offscreen canvas keyed by (events, zoom window, css size, dpr); per frame blit it and draw the playhead + range only. Cache --accent in the token module and invalidate on theme change.
top_perf_items.risk: Low. Pure render refactor behind the existing draw call; the zoom window is already an explicit key.

top_perf_items.area: Player - per-note allocation in the visualizer render loop (renderer/player/visualizer.js:229, 233, 88)
top_perf_items.issue: createLinearGradient plus colour-string concatenation per visible note per frame, a beginPath/4x arcTo/fill path per note, a per-key strokeRect for the keybed, and fresh [0,2,4,5,7,9,11] / [1,3,6,8,10] array literals allocated inside _noteGeom which runs per note per frame. Hundreds of allocations per frame feeding a GC that runs on the same thread that must service progress packets and dispatch keypresses.
top_perf_items.fix: Precompute two gradients per channel colour at load/setStyle time (or flat fills below a size threshold), fillRect for small notes, one batched path for all keybed separators, and hoist the pitch-class tests to module-level lookup tables.
top_perf_items.risk: Low-medium. Visual output must stay identical; the gradient is described in-code as subtle, so a flat fill is an acceptable fallback if the precomputed gradients look off.

top_perf_items.area: Editor - refresh() reallocates both canvases and repaints everything on every edit (renderer/review/review.js:275-278, 139)
top_perf_items.issue: Every velocity change, delete, nudge or transpose runs Math.max(...notes.map(n=>n.end)) plus resizeRoll() and resizeWave(), each of which reassigns canvas.width/height (a fresh cleared surface) and does an O(all notes) repaint. The #zoom slider fires this per pixel of travel. The spread of every note end / every pitch also throws RangeError past ~100k arguments, so a very large transcription hard-fails on its first refresh.
top_perf_items.fix: Split geometry-invalidating refresh from repaint-only (the drag path already proves the cheap path works); track maxEnd incrementally with a loop, never a spread; reallocate the backing store only when the pixel size changed; rAF-coalesce the scroll and zoom repaints.
top_perf_items.risk: Medium. Touching the central refresh path; needs care that duration widening, bounds recompute and control gating still happen where they must.

top_perf_items.area: Editor - playback note triggering and undo checkpoints (review.js:642, 88, 765)
top_perf_items.issue: triggerNotes() walks the ENTIRE note array every rAF tick (~60/s) although only a ~16ms window can match, and it is deliberately outside the draw throttle - 600k comparisons/second on a 10k-note song. Separately, holding an arrow key pushes one full-document clone onto the undo stack per OS repeat, blowing through the 80-entry cap in about two seconds and discarding real history.
top_perf_items.fix: Keep notes sorted by start and advance a cursor (binary-search on seek); coalesce autorepeat nudges into one checkpoint per key-hold using the same dirtied-flag trick as the drag path; move to inverse-operation patches instead of whole-array snapshots.
top_perf_items.risk: Medium. Undo semantics are user-visible; the id-keyed selection model must keep working across restore.

top_perf_items.area: Main process - IPC fan-out of high-rate log/progress streams (electron/main.js:113 broadcast, forge-runner.js:279, forge-provisioner.js:117, sidecar.js:117)
top_perf_items.issue: broadcast() rebuilds the subframe list and structured-clone-serialises the payload once per frame for every event. The forge pump splits on \r, so an MSST tqdm bar or a yt-dlp download emits hundreds to thousands of 'lines' per stage, each becoming one emit -> one broadcast -> N frame sends. pip output during provisioning does the same, plus a synchronous fs.writeSync per chunk. This is the hottest main-thread path exactly while a transcription or a download is running, i.e. while the user may also be playing notes into a game.
top_perf_items.fix: Cache the frame list (invalidate on frame-created/destroyed), batch log lines on a ~100ms timer into one array payload, throttle progress to ~10-20Hz, drop lines that differ only in a percentage, and tee the provisioner log through a write stream.
top_perf_items.risk: Low. The renderer already appends lines in order; batching preserves order and the monotonic percent clamp is unaffected.

top_perf_items.area: Library scanning blocking the main process (electron/library.js:26, main.js:130 listMidis)
top_perf_items.issue: A recursive synchronous directory walk with one fs.statSync per file, up to 4000 files, executed directly inside the library:list IPC handler - and a second, differently-ruled synchronous scanner for app:listMidis. The whole app (all IPC, all window input) freezes for the duration, on a cold cache or a slow disk that is seconds. library-changed fires after every finished Forge job and every Editor export, and the renderer re-lists on it.
top_perf_items.fix: One async scanner (fs.promises + withFileTypes, batched stats), cached per root and invalidated by mtime/library-changed, feeding both the Library tab and the Player picker. Return incrementally so the list paints as it fills.
top_perf_items.risk: Low-medium. Must preserve the melody-sibling folding (_balanced/_detailed into their primary, orphans kept), the skip set, the depth/file caps and the truncated flag.

top_perf_items.area: Whole-app synchronous persistence (electron/settings.js:69, renderer/player/app.js:164, shell.js:282, overlay.js:139)
top_perf_items.issue: settings.merge() stringifies and writes the entire settings file synchronously and then returns a full JSON round-trip deep clone; callers include overlay move/resize (every 400ms of dragging Perch, with config() rebuilt twice per save), app:setUi, app:setPerformance and the forge-path paths. In the renderer, saveSettings() stringifies the whole object (playlist up to 200 entries) to localStorage from ~30 handlers including #tempo 'input', #note-color 'input' and #fall-speed 'input' - a synchronous write per pointermove - and the shell's colour picker fires deriveAccent + 35 cross-document setProperty writes + one IPC invoke per input event.
top_perf_items.fix: Dirty-flag both stores and flush once per ~1s and on quit (temp+rename async write); return the live object or a shallow snapshot; split continuous inputs so the visual change happens on 'input' (rAF-coalesced) and persistence happens on 'change', which the percent slider already does correctly.
top_perf_items.risk: Low. Needs a guaranteed flush on before-quit and on window close so nothing is lost.

top_perf_items.area: Forge - whole-file decode and main-thread peak scan per input (renderer/forge/forge.js:365, 379)
top_perf_items.issue: Every setInput fetches the entire audio file into an ArrayBuffer, decodeAudioData's it, and then linearly scans channel 0 into 4096 buckets on the main thread - ~80M samples for a 30-minute file. This runs on every automatic queue advance, so a long batch repeats whole-file I/O plus a transient decoded buffer several times the file size, freezing the UI between jobs. The AudioContext is never released.
top_perf_items.fix: Move decode + bucketing into a Worker (or OfflineAudioContext downsampling) posting back only the peak pairs; skip the load entirely while a batch is auto-advancing or the preview panel is collapsed; suspend/close the context when idle.
top_perf_items.risk: Low. waveToken already guards stale completions, so an async worker fits the existing model.

top_perf_items.area: Forge - waveform repaint on every playback tick and every drag move (forge.js:736, 752, 783, 217)
top_perf_items.issue: #preview-audio 'timeupdate' (4-15Hz) runs the full drawWaveform - background, axis, up to 12 grid columns with fillText, a per-CSS-pixel peak path, selection overlay, playhead - just to move a 1px line, and calls css() (getComputedStyle on documentElement) 6-8 times per repaint. Range-drag pointermove additionally writes both time inputs, revalidates and repaints per event, and window 'resize' is bound straight to drawWaveform with no throttle.
top_perf_items.fix: Static layers offscreen + blit; rAF-coalesce the drag (store the pending range, apply once per frame); cached tokens; ResizeObserver on the wave shell instead of a raw window resize handler. Also fix the peak indexing so a zoomed-out view aggregates min/max across covered buckets instead of skipping them.
top_perf_items.risk: Low. The bucket-aggregation change is a visual improvement (real peaks stop being dropped).

top_perf_items.area: Self MIDI - library list rebuild per keystroke (renderer/audition/audition.js:128, 155, 159, 577)
top_perf_items.issue: The search input is undebounced, so every keystroke filters, copies and fully re-sorts up to 4000 entries (localeCompare for name/folder), then tears down and rebuilds 300 rows - each row an innerHTML parse plus two querySelector calls plus two listener closures, i.e. ~600 listener allocations discarded on the next keypress.
top_perf_items.fix: Debounce ~120ms, sort once per sort-order change rather than per render, reuse row nodes, build the two child nodes directly, and use one delegated click + one delegated contextmenu on the host reading data-path. This is the same virtualised-list primitive the new Library tab needs anyway.

top_perf_items.area: Self MIDI + Player - per-note DOM reads and linear seek scans (audition.js:317, 225; app.js:1856)
top_perf_items.issue: playNote() reads four DOM controls (volume, sustain, pitch, instrument) per scheduled note inside the audio scheduler, so a dense passage does hundreds of getElementById+property reads per 120ms tick. cursorFor() is a linear scan from index 0 and runs on every seek-slider 'input' event. In the Player, viz.seek() resets the cull cursor to 0, so each mousemove of a scrubber drag forces the next render to walk the whole event array from the start, on top of 30Hz seek IPC.
top_perf_items.fix: Mirror the four control values into module variables maintained by their existing change handlers; binary-search the cursor in both players; coalesce drag seeks to the render loop instead of to every mousemove.
top_perf_items.risk: Low. Mirrored state must be initialised from the restored prefs at boot, or the first note plays at the wrong volume.

top_perf_items.issue: dataUriBuffer() decodes base64 with atob and then copies byte-by-byte in a JS loop - multiple megabytes per instrument copied one charCodeAt at a time on the main thread during 'Loading <instrument>...'. Decodes are awaited one sample at a time, serialising an otherwise parallel off-thread operation, so total wait is the sum rather than the max. sampleForPitch() then does Object.keys(bank) plus a linear scan per note played.
top_perf_items.fix: fetch(dataUri).arrayBuffer() (or a bulk typed-array conversion), Promise.all the decodes with progress reported as each settles, and build a 128-entry pitch->sample table once per bank in prepare().
top_perf_items.risk: Low. Keep the 2-instrument LRU eviction and the token-based cancellation exactly as they are.

top_perf_items.area: rAF loops that keep waking when they will not draw (audition.js:368, player/app.js:1966, review.js:651)
top_perf_items.issue: Because renderer backgrounding is disabled app-wide, rAF is not slowed when the window is occluded. Self MIDI's tick() re-arms itself at full rate even when the budget is Infinity (hidden or off-screen), and the Player's drawBudgetMs() re-reads two dataset attributes plus a Number() on every wakeup - the code itself measured ~500 wakeups/sec. The Editor reads dataset.onscreen but never listens for the 'midi-studio:onscreen' event, so returning to the tab shows a stale, possibly wrongly-sized canvas until the playhead moves a pixel.
top_perf_items.fix: Park the loop entirely when the budget is Infinity (drive position updates off the existing 120ms scheduler) and resume from the onscreen/visibilitychange events; cache the budget and invalidate it from those events plus a MutationObserver on data-drawms; give the Editor the same onscreen listener plus a resize+repaint on wake.
top_perf_items.risk: Low, but the wake path must be exercised: a parked loop that never resumes is a frozen tab.

top_perf_items.area: Settings modal keeps the active tab's draw loop alive (renderer/shell/shell.css:105)
top_perf_items.issue: body.modal-open .tabframe uses visibility:hidden, which keeps the iframe laid out, composited and running, and does NOT flip data-onscreen (markVisibility keys only off .is-active). With backgroundThrottling off, an Editor or Self MIDI piano roll keeps producing frames nobody can see for as long as Settings is open.
top_perf_items.fix: Have the settings open/close path stamp data-onscreen='0'/'1' (or fold modal-open into the visibility scheduler) so covered panels park their loops.
top_perf_items.risk: Low. Must still repaint on close, via the same wake event as a tab switch.

top_perf_items.area: Per-frame style reads and layout thrash in paint and drag paths (review.js:207, 403; audition.js:503, 489; tokens.css:218; resize.js:128)
top_perf_items.issue: The Editor reads getComputedStyle --accent inside the per-note draw loop (thousands of style resolutions/second with a large selection) and calls getBoundingClientRect twice per pointermove during note drags, interleaved with canvas writes. Self MIDI spreads a fresh pitch array through Math.min/Math.max per draw and strokes each grid line separately. The indeterminate progress bar animates margin-left (a layout property, ignoring the draw budget entirely). The divider's keyboard nudge does a full localStorage read-parse-stringify-write plus a synthetic global 'resize' per autorepeat tick - a redraw storm by construction.
top_perf_items.fix: Cached tokens; cache the rect on pointerdown for the gesture; precompute low/high at load; batch grid lines into two paths; animate transform:translateX with will-change; debounce the nudge's persist and resize dispatch to one trailing call.
